title: Dairy-Free Cinnamon Maple Cupcakes
shortDescription: Warm cinnamon maple cupcakes with a creamy vanilla swirl, ready in about 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These dairy-free cinnamon maple cupcakes taste like a warm fall morning. I mixed real maple syrup with maple extract so the flavor stays strong even after baking. Ground cinnamon goes into the batter, not just the frosting, so every bite has that cozy spice. The frosting is a creamy vanilla swirl made with dairy-free butter, so it still pipes tall and holds its shape. I tested this batch in my home kitchen on a cold Sunday. The cupcakes came out soft, moist, and not too sweet, with a light maple smell as they baked. This is a good pick for fall parties, lunchboxes, or anytime you want a cozy cupcake without dairy.
ingredients: 1 cup dairy-free butter, softened, for frosting
1 to 2 tbsp unsweetened almond milk, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a medium bowl.
Beat dairy-free butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in maple syrup and maple extract.
Add the dry mix in three parts, alternating with almond milk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly into liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack to cool fully.
Beat dairy-free butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar and vanilla extract.
Add almond milk one tablespoon at a time until the frosting is smooth and pipeable.
Pipe frosting high in a swirl on each cooled cupcake, then dust with a pinch of cinnamon.
tips: Use real maple syrup, not pancake syrup, for the truest maple flavor.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting so the swirl holds its shape.
Room temperature eggs and dairy-free butter mix smoother and rise better.
If your frosting looks too soft, chill it 10 minutes before piping.

faq.question: Can I use only maple extract instead of maple syrup?
faq.answer: No, keep both. Maple syrup adds moisture and mild sweetness, while the extract boosts the maple flavor without extra liquid.

faq.question: What dairy-free butter works best for this recipe?
faq.answer: A block style dairy-free butter with at least 70 percent fat works best. It creams up smoother than spreadable tub versions.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost the day you plan to serve them.

faq.question: Why is my frosting too thin to pipe a tall swirl?
faq.answer: You likely added too much almond milk too fast. Add powdered sugar in small amounts to thicken it back up before piping.

conclusion: These cinnamon maple cupcakes bring warm spice and real maple flavor to a simple dairy-free bake. The creamy vanilla swirl on top keeps them feeling like a bakery treat, not a substitute recipe.
